arguments.name: Allison's Easter confession is a stunning testimony
arguments.conclusion: Dale Allison's statement that the disciples saw Jesus and that he will be in church next Easter is a stunning, memorable confession from a critical scholar.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas (reporting Dale Allison)
premises: Allison writes: 'I believe that the disciples saw Jesus and that he saw them and next Easter will find me in church.'
Habermas finds this stunning after reading Allison for years.
Habermas ranks this comment as probably the best of the examples he could give.

st1.quote: That was a real stunning comment after I read uh Dale for years.

st2.quote: I believe that the disciples saw Jesus and that he saw them and next Easter will find me in church.

st4.quote: That was a real stunning comment after I read uh Dale for years.

st6.quote: that one by Dale probably takes the cake.

or1.quote: I believe that the disciples saw Jesus and that he saw them and next Easter will find me in church.
or1.why: Habermas's argument is essentially a report of Allison's own prior statement; the variant is Habermas's framing of it as a 'stunning' testimony.

or2.quote: That was a real stunning comment after I read uh Dale for years.
or2.why: Adds Habermas's personal reaction and ranking of the quote, not new evidence.

arguments.weakest_link: The inference from 'Allison said something striking' to any evidential conclusion about the resurrection is unstated and unsupported.
arguments.develop_next: State explicitly what the quote is evidence for (e.g., that even critical scholars concede the disciples' experience) and cite the exact page in Allison's volume.

arguments.name: Gundry's soma work targets Bultmann's view of the body
arguments.conclusion: Robert Gundry was one of the first to write on the subject, and his book 'Soma' directly takes on Bultmann's influential view of the body.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: Gundry wrote a treatment of human beings called 'Soma,' the Greek word for body.
Gundry is primarily taking on Bultmann's very influential view of the body.

st1.quote: Now, Gundry was one of the first to write on the subject.

st2.quote: it's called soma the Greek word for body and he's taking on Bultmann primarily.

st4.quote: he specifically wrote his the treatment of human beings um you know, it's it's called soma the Greek word for body and he's taking on Bultmann primarily.

arguments.prior_art: Robert Gundry, Soma in Biblical Theology, 1976; Rudolf Bultmann, Theology of the New Testament, 1948

or1.quote: he specifically wrote his the treatment of human beings um you know, it's it's called soma the Greek word for body
or1.why: A variant of the standard scholarly observation about Gundry's Soma; Habermas adds the framing of it as targeting Bultmann.

or2.why: No new evidence beyond the existing book.

arguments.weakest_link: The claim that Gundry 'takes on Bultmann primarily' is asserted without citing anything from Soma.
arguments.develop_next: Quote the specific passage in Soma where Gundry engages Bultmann's view of the body.

arguments.name: Multiple scholars affirm strong bodily resurrection terms
arguments.conclusion: Several notable scholars—Tom Wright, Michael Licona, and Robert Gundry—make strong statements affirming the bodily resurrection, similar to Cook's.
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
premises: Tom Wright has comments just like Cook's.
Robert Gundry, in his book on Soma, makes similar strong bodily statements.

st1.quote: So, does um uh Gundry in his book on Soma.

st2.quote: Uh Tom Wright has some comments just like that.

st4.quote: those are startling comments to me when guys jump right in and say that.

st6.quote: So, does um uh Gundry in his book on Soma.

st8.quote: Uh Tom Wright has some comments just like that. So, does Michael Licona. So, does um uh Gundry in his book on Soma.

arguments.prior_art: N.T. Wright, The Resurrection of the Son of God, 2003; Michael Licona, The Resurrection of Jesus, 2010

or1.quote: So, does um uh Gundry in his book on Soma.
or1.why: A variant of the existing scholarly consensus; Habermas aggregates named scholars rather than making a new argument.

or2.why: No new evidence or data introduced.

arguments.weakest_link: The alleged 'similar comments' from Wright, Licona and Gundry are never quoted, so the convergence claim is unsupported.
arguments.develop_next: Quote the actual sentence from each scholar showing the strong bodily-resurrection affirmation.
